newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kidnapped German in Yemen says being treated well.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped German in Yemen says being treated well.

text.p: A German tour guide kidnapped along with six other German tourists in southeastern Yemen told a Hamburg radio station on Thursday they were being treated "fairly well."
Ulrich Boettcher, tour guide for the group of motorcyclists seized by gunmen on Monday, told NDR2 radio that their kidnappers were demanding $12 million from the Yemen government.
"We were kidnapped by a group of about 50 locals four days ago," Boettcher said, adding that he was calling from a satellite telephone from the Mokalla region in eastern Yemen.

"The assailaints are armed with Kalashnikov rifles and high-calibre automatic weapons," Boettcher said. "The kidnappers are poorly prepared for the further course of the kidnapping. They appear confused and are very emotional in their actions."
NDR2 said Boettcher's voice was confirmed by his father in Hamburg.

In the transcript of the brief interview that was abruptly cut off after several questions, Boettcher said the kidnappers allowed him to make the call because they hoped the German embassy in Yemen would intervene.
"They are afraid, despite assurances from the Yemen Interior Ministry, that they will use violence to end the kidnapping," Boettcher said. "They react very nervously to airplane noises here."

Asked if they were being treated well, Boettcher said: "We are being treated relatively well at the moment." He said the biggest threat to the Germans came at the start of the kidnapping on Monday when they were threated with weapons.
Asked if he had had contact with officials in Yemen, Boettcher started to answer, but suddenly said:
"Unfortunately I have to interrupt this conversation right now," he said.
Earlier, the German Foreign Ministry said it had appealed to Yemen's security services to do all they can to free the seven tourists.
The ministry said Yemen President Ali Abdullah Saleh had met German ambassador Helga Graefin Strachwitz and had personally taken on the case, setting up three emergency committees.
The ministry statement came as Yemeni security forces laid siege to southeastern parts of the country to help free the men.
They were seized by gunmen in the Wadi al-Dabaat between Mahra and Hadramaut provinces on Monday.

Official sources said the kidnappers, all local tribesmen, wanted to put pressure on the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them smuggled cars brought in from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states.
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil companies have kidnapped dozens of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
